description: Guru Purnima — a themed treasury of teachings gathered by the Śrī Chaitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha.

articles.title: Vedavyas Muni - Shaktyavesh Avatar
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: On this most auspicious Tithi of Guru-purnima, the appearance day of Srila Krishna-dvaipayan Vedavyasa Muni and disappearance day of Srila Sanatan Goswami, Srila Gurumaharaj narrates the life of both the exalted personalities in brief. Specifically, he emphasizes on the main teachings one needs to accept from their lives. Vedavyas Muni is Shaktyavesh avatar of the Lord, non-different from the Lord Himself. He was a very learned person who wrote so many scriptures. In spite of writing so many scriptures, he did not get inner peace in his heart. On the order of his Gurudev, Srila Narad Goswami, when he sang the glories of the Supreme Lord, he experienced the highest bliss in his heart.

blocks.text: Today is Guru-purnima and along with it the disappearance day of Srila Sanatana Goswami. Last week, we saw Slovenian devotees at the conference. That day, I had to speak in Hindi to satisfy the devotees, our secretary Pujyapada Tridandi Swami, Bhakti Vigyan Bharati Maharaj spoke in Bengali. The people from Bengal cannot understand Hindi. That is the difficulty. So I announced on that day that I will remember the glories again, for the foreign devotees. Although, our Param Gurudeva, as I have heard from our Gurudev, when he was speaking in Madras Gaudiya Math, he spoke in Bengali. At that time Bengali listeners were there. Afterwards some dignitaries came from the city. Their mother tongue was Tamil. They could not understand Bengali. They could understand English only. Literate persons were there. So our Brahmacharis and Sanyasis approached Srila Prabhupad and requested him to speak in English because there were some local devotees, they would not be able to understand if speaks in Bengali. But our Param Gurudeva still was speaking in Bengali. They approached him repeatedly and requested again but he did not speak in English, he spoke in Bengali only. Afterwards when they (Brahmacharis and Sanyasis) were too much eager, then Srila Prabhupad told them, “I have not heard from my Gurudev that Bhakti can be propagated and transmitted by language, I have not heard this. It can be transmitted by any language, if the listener is sincere.

Because these words are transcendental words, coming from the transcendental realm, they will touch your soul. The soul is also transcendental, whether you understand or not, the vibration itself will create something in your mind and your eternal nature will be manifested, causeless devotion. But if you hear in your own language, very fluently, very nicely, but his (speakers) ego is here in his honor and (if he has) mundane interests for what he is speaking, (if the) ultimate end is something else, not known, then you will not be benefitted, spiritually. You may understand it; but there will be no actual benefit. So I never heard from our Gurudev that, through language, devotion can be transmitted to any other person.” I heard it from our Guru Maharaj that our Param Gurudev used to speak English very well. He is a learned person. Intentionally he did not speak (in English). Only to teach the Bramhacharis that if you have the desire to deliver a good speech and (earn) a good name in this world, your spiritual life will be lost and the end result will be something else. It should be for the satisfaction of Krishna. You have to pray for His grace.

Day before yesterday was Guru-purnima. What is the meaning of Guru-purnima? Full moon day of the month of Ashadh. Ashadh is a Bengali calendar month. Vedvyasa Muni appeared on this day. So the whole of India, even outside India, those who have belief in Sanatana Dharma they perform worship of Vedvyasa Muni everywhere. Vedvyasa Muni appeared on an island, island means Dvipa. His complexion was black, he is known as Krishna Dvaipayana. Krishna means black complexion and Dvaipayana means born in Dvipa, Krishna Dvipa. Vedvyasa means one who has expanded the Vedas or divided the Vedas into four categories. An ordinary person cannot do this. There is power, spiritual power behind him. (He is) Saktyavesh Avatar. That power is given by the Lord to him. He appeared accepting Parashara Rishi, a very powerful Rishi and Satyavati. He dedicated himself to all the spiritual matters and he said to his mother, ‘’I shall not be with you, but whenever you remember me I shall come to you. You are not to contact me by letter or through anybody. If you remember me under any difficult circumstance, I shall understand it and I shall be able to come to you.’’ On that condition, he remained away from his mother and divided the Vedas and wrote 18 Puranas. Also he wrote Vedanta, the most adored scripture of the Gyanis, philosophical aspects you will get. He wrote Mahabharata and Gita, Gita is there within Mahabharata. He is respected by all in India whatever group it may be, Karmi, Gyani, Yogi, Bhakta, everyone. So today’s Tithi is called Guru-purnima. He is worshipped everywhere.

Vedvyasa Muni has got so much power. Something should be spoken about him. He is not an ordinary man. By accepting him as father Dhritrastra, Pandu and Vidur appeared, but Dhritrastra was born blind. During the Kurukshetra war he was there in his house, and out of affection, Vedvyasa Muni imparted power to Sanjay to see everything in the battlefield, the things that are happening there and he used to speak about it to Dhritarastra. An ordinary saint cannot impart such power. By the imparted power of Vedvyasa Muni Sanjay saw everything in the battle field and spoke about Gita to Dhritarastra. At the end of the battle, so many millions were killed. Their women had an extreme experience of grief and separation. Then Vedvyasa Muni told them to not be disheartened. “I will show (you all) your husband and other relatives. See they are alright.” The grief stricken women saw their dead husband and dead relatives. Can any person do this?

But one thing we have to think about is this. After writing so many Granthas (dividing the Vedas, writing Mahabharat and Puranas) he could not get actual bliss in his heart. That you have to understand. To show the world, (He thought) “You worldly people may have some vanity, you are very learned persons. You also study scriptures and you write books. Can you write what I did? I did so much. Human beings they want money. Without money they cannot maintain their family. We cannot do anything. So I wrote Artha-shastra, how to earn money for their benefit. All the human beings, conditioned souls they want their desires to be fulfilled. For that reason, I have written Kama-shastra. How can you fulfill these desires? This body is non-eternal, it has birth, it has death and after death how can you get in this world or in any other world, a good birth, a peaceful birth? For that I wrote Dharma-shastra. Whatever they want I have given them. They should be happy and in return I should also be happy, feel happiness within my heart. But I have no happiness. My mind is not at peace, it is not in peace or in bliss. So much I did for the human beings for their benefit but I myself could not get any actual bliss? Bliss means cessation of disturbances, permanent bliss is in Supreme Lord. I do not know why I have not got it. What is the reason?” Then he went to Badarinarayan and took shelter of his Gurudev Narada, “Kindly show me the path. I did so much for the worldly people. In return I surely must have got peace and bliss, some happiness, but I have not achieved it, what is the reason? I cannot understand.”
“What did you do?”
“I wrote all these things, Dharma-shastra, Artha-shastra, Kama-shastra.”
Then Narada said,

“Whatever you did was bad, abominable work. All the conditioned souls have got this sort of non-eternal desires with non-eternal ego. They want money, they want their desires to be fulfilled, and they want some material enjoyment in this world and other worlds. This is non-eternal. You have given them trouble, then trouble will come to you in reaction. You cannot get peace. You have not given peace. You have not even given bliss, you have given disturbance. You have instructed them, you have persuaded them for non-eternal things, non-eternal enjoyment. A great wrong you have done.”
“I have also spoken about emancipation, about salvation.”
Then Narada Goswami said, “This is far more dangerous. You have deprived them of getting Krishna-prem for eternal time.”

(Guruji explains) You want to merge yourself with the impersonal formless Brahma. You are committing suicide; to merge yourself into Paramatma, which is further worse than Brahmananda, ‘Brahma-sayujya’. Nobody can get actual Brahma-sayujya without the grace of the Supreme Lord. The Supreme Lord is All-powerful, He is the giver. When Chatuhshan performed penance and wanted Brahmananda, but accepting the Supreme Lord as the Supreme, worshipping the Supreme Lord, they prayed for salvation then they got it. Without accepting Him you get zero, nothing. You can get nothing. Here in this world as long as human beings are here with their senses, thinking, feeling and willing, (that is while the soul, which is sachidanand, is present in the body) so you will get help or advice and everything. When the soul leaves from the body then what can you give? Can you give anything? Can a dead body give anything? What can it give? Give one instance where a dead body has given anything. And the Supreme Lord is the cause of all infinite particles, atomic parts, jivas, living beings. As long as that anu sachidananda, atomic part of chidananda exists in the body, so long it will give you and can give satisfaction to others, others can give satisfaction to him. When that leaves your body nobody will touch your body and if they touch they will have to take a bath.

All the jivas are coming from Brahma, not from Abrahma. Nothing can be because of something. These living beings, from where have they come? From inert matter? Without consciousness? If there is no consciousness (in the source) how can consciousness come? If you rub two pieces of wood, fire comes out, emerges. (If someone says,) “Oh there is no fire in wood, it comes because of rubbing (the wood together).” No (it is not like that). Fire is already there. Pancha-mahabhuta, earth, water, fire, air, sky, all are there. By rubbing wood fire appears. Something is coming from nothing, this is not correct. Wrong statement. From the Supreme Lord we have come. We are in the Supreme Lord, we are by the Supreme Lord.

Now Narada Goswami told, “You have done more harm, the highest harm to the living beings by saying about Brahmananda for merging oneself into a formless Brahman or Paramatma. In front of Prem that Brahmananda is nothing. What have you done? You have not spoken about the glories of the Supreme Lord. The Supreme Lord is all Bliss, He can take the initiative, He is Sacchidananda, He is All Powerful, All Existence, All Knowledge, All Bliss.”

(Guruji explains) By His grace if He wants to, anybody who takes actual shelter to Him, He will appear. He will not think about the status of a human being, whether they are birds or beasts. The person who takes shelter to Him— daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te We go through Gita, we do not accept Gita. (Then) What is the use of going through Gita? He has got no differentiation—

“I am equal to all. Even if an animal takes shelter to Me I shall rescue him from Maya.”
But if you go by a challenging mood, by taking this human birth where the Supreme Lord has given you the discriminating power between good and bad, right and wrong, eternal and non-eternal, then you will be deprived. You can accept eternal truth. You have to give up the challenging mood, if you do not do this then you will be deprived. Other living beings have got no such discriminating power.

There is one group which are Mayavadi, they say ‘soham, soham, soham’ — I am that Brahman. (They believe) “By soham we become Bhagavan. Bhagavan sometimes becomes Bhagavan. Sometime He is not Bhagavan.” This is not true. Bhagavan is always Bhagavan. (Mayavadi’s think), “Sometimes when he is enveloped by maya He becomes jiva and after practicing soham He becomes Bhagavan.” This is irrational talk. Bhagavan is Absolute. Absolute is Absolute, always Absolute. There cannot be any state of non-existence of the Supreme Lord. With a challenging mood, if you go by your finite intellect, very negligible, finite mental capacity then your whole spiritual life will be destroyed. The knowledge will come through Supreme Lord’s preceptorial channel. It is the only path. There is no other path. If you go with your vanity, with ego, you will remain here all the time in this world. You cannot go there. There is no equal to Him or more than Him. He is Asamurdhva (there is no one equal or higher than Him). Without His grace nobody can cross over birth and death, and the threefold afflictions. You have committed an offence at His Lotus feet. Jiva is part of His potency, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu said marginal potency or apara potency. The Supreme Lord is the possessor of the potency. Anything produced by the potency also belongs to the Supreme Lord. I have no hold over my body, this body belongs to Supreme Lord, the astral body (subtle body) belongs to the Supreme Lord, atma belongs to the Supreme Lord. According to Gita, atma comes from the aparaprakriti of the Supreme Lord. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu says tatastha-shakti. A philosophical solution. You are a part of the potency, not part of the substance and you have eternal relation. That you have to understand.

All the Vaishnava Acharyas, they have warned us that if you give up this (relation, meaning if you forget this relation) then your whole human life will be futile. tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṁ padaṁ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ divīva cakṣur ātatam. Daily you meditate on this. What is the meaning? The lotus feet of Vishnu are eternal, sadā paśyanti - means always observing. The realized souls, emancipated souls are always observing the lotus feet of Vishnu, they must remain always (eternally) and the observer must be always (eternal). Then always observation can be possible. In Rig Veda it is said, padaṁ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ divīva cakṣur ātatam. How to see Him? By a challenging mood? Brahma, he is the creator of the living beings in this world, this universe. He could not recognize Krishna. From where you have come, that you will recognize Krishna and Krishna’s absolute counterpart, the devotees? Impossible. Some say that Brahma made this as a pastime. Brahma, we remember him in our preceptorial channel. Yes, he is our Guru. We always remember. But why has Vedavyasa Muni not written in his book that Brahma had made this pastime? There is some underlying intention behind this. These conditioned souls will misunderstand this. You should understand that Brahma, the creator by his own power, endeavor, he could not get any knowledge of Vrindavan Dham, any knowledge of cowherd boys, any knowledge of Gopa-gopis, Krishna. When Krishna Himself was present, Brahma could not understand. (Vedvyas Muni said,) “To show these to conditioned souls, I do not want to say Brahma made the pastimes and make it less important. You conditioned souls make that sort of mentality of a challenging mood, where is God and what you are?”

When our Parampujyapada Swami Maharaj was there in America one young boy came. He said, “Swamiji, I do not believe God.” Then Swami Maharaj said, “Who has given you the power to say that I do not believe God? How long you can speak like this? How long you will be here? You have got this vanity, when the life will be taken out from the body, can you speak? Your speaking power is given by the Supreme Lord. As you do not want to worship the Supreme Lord and you want to enjoy life He created this universe and all these eighty four lakh species to fulfill your desire and that also He is fulfilling. If you were just alone you could do nothing. How long will you have this vanity?’’ Therefore this challenging mood should be totally removed, if there is any tinge of a challenging mood, you will be deprived from the devotional school of thought, actual spiritually. You will not get this. The Supreme Lord is descending through a preceptorial channel. Our Bhakti Siddhant Saraswati Goswami Thakur, will he speak a lie? Bhaktivinoda Thakur, will he speak a lie? For what, they have come? They were sent by Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Because these human beings have got no understanding, by their own capacity they cannot understand the writings of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Shada Goswamis, Srimad Bhagavatam. So many pseudo sects have cropped up. Nobody understood Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu sent Bhakti Siddhant Saraswati Goswami Thakur. Now we can speak like this. But when Bhakti Siddhant Saraswati Goswami Thakur was present, he performed so much penance here in Mayapur, so much powerful penance. Those persons who went to talk with him to refute his Suddha Bhakti, when they saw him they could not utter a word. When they saw him and heard him they could not say anything. He is not an ordinary person. He is sent by Supreme Lord. Therefore our Param Gurudeva, you will find when starting his sermons, his speeches, he advises us to make obeisances to the preceptorial channel. If you do not believe in him then you will be deprived of your emancipation from this world. By taking shelter to them, go on worshipping, what will you get? You will get (the love of Him) and you will give it to others also. And without that if you go with a challenging mood, with our finite intellect, finite mental capacity, if you go and know Him then God will become finite. He is not finite. He is infinite.
Now, you see, Our Narada Goswami told him, “You have not spoken about Krishna”.
(Vedvyas Muni,) “I spoke about Krishna.”
“Where?”
“In Mahabharata, Gita.”

“There your end (goal) is something else, mukti, emancipation not Krishna. You have to sing the glories of Krishna for Krishna’s sake then you will have attachment to Krishna. If Krishna is satisfied then you will be satisfied. You have written there with the purpose to get emancipation, salvation. But that will not give you peace. You have to sing the glories of Krishna for His satisfaction knowing Him, I am of Him, I am a part of His potency”.

And by getting the grace of His Grace Incarnate form of Krishna, Narada Goswami, who imparted four verses, by that imparted power Vedvyasa Muni saw that (actual reality). He saw everything and after seeing he wrote Srimad Bhagavatam twelve centos (Skandas) by which Krishna was satisfied. Then he had bliss. That (place) is there, in Bhadrinarayana. Badrinarayana temple it is not built by Gaudiya Math. After Badrinarayana, above one thousand feet, there is an ashram. Everybody goes there to make obeisances. It is not built by Gaudiya Math. I have been to that place once with Guru Maharaj. Guru Maharaj sat there and he read Bhagavatam and the six or seven persons that were there, in that cave, a very big cave. After getting peace, Vedavyasa Muni instructed Sukadeva Goswami and Sukadeva Goswami gave up Brahmananda and became Krishna Premi and got Krishna-prem. In Sukartala, where all the Rishi-munis were present, even Agastya Muni who drank anocean, Parashurama one of Dashavatar all were present. All stood up when Sukadev Goswami came and they heard Srimad Bhagavatam from him for seven days. Before Sukadev Goswami’s arrival Pariksit Maharaj was puzzled because the Munis and Rishis assembled there were suggesting to him quite different paths. Then he remembered Krishna and prayed, “I was related with Pandavas. Kindly give me mercy, kindly help me, kindly have grace with me. After some days I shall be killed by a snake bite.” Then He (Krishna) sent Sukadeva Goswami. After listening for seven days, without taking food, without sleeping, can you think about this without taking water for seven days? Sukadeva Goswami is giving Krishna Himself, through transcendental sound, to Pariksit Maharaj and he is accepting. After seven days, transcendental sound, the Supreme Lord appeared in his heart and all the worldly things from the heart were removed. Where is such a speaker, actual speaker? Where is such actual listener, so that one can get the actual good?

Now you see, in this matter we have to think about Sanatan Goswami. Today is Sanatan Goswami’s disappearance day. Because time is short what can be done? Long subject. After writing Bhagavat, Vedvyasa Muni got bliss. By his life he has taught us if you go through Bhagavat, a bonafide Bhagavat and if you are bonafide, you will not be deprived. It is said in the Gita, na hi kalyāṇa-kṛt kaścid durgatiṁ tāta gacchati. Krishna is telling, emphatically. If anybody is sincere, he will not be deceived. Krishna has said, he will not be deceived. Krishna will send His own man. He will come and contact the conditioned souls. That preceptorial channel is given by Saraswati Goswami Thakur, Bhaktivinoda Thakur, we should have firm faith in it and believe Him. Give your life for it and see whether you get the actual peace or not. You can see that afterwards. If you give up, you will go to hell, you will come back to this world again. When you become averse to Sri Krishna, nobody will come to help you. His external potency (mahamaya) will envelop you and then you will do something by which you will be enveloped in this world.
Srila Prabhupad has written in his Vaishnava ke’ Kirtan,
He has not cited any incident from Bhagavatam or Chaitanya Charitamrita, he has advised to go through the teachings given to Sanatan Goswami by Mahaprabhu with utmost care.

You should hear about Sanatana Goswami, what question he asked to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and what were the teachings given to him. His life is full of teachings. We have to go through his life, it is written by Kavikarnapura, the son of Shivananda Sen. Sanatan Goswami is dearest to Rupa Manjari. Bhaktivinoda Thakur is a Rupanugavara, those who are subservient to Rupa Goswami. Bhaktivinoda Thakur is the best amongst them. In a spiritual sense, Rupa Goswami is Shrestha (superior). Sanatan Goswami, in the worldly sense, is the elder brother of him. But in the spiritual sense, Rupa Goswami is the highest. He is Rupa-manjari. Sanatan Goswami is under him. Sanatan Goswami is Rati-manjari or Lavanga-manjari. Also Sanatan of Chatuhshan entered into him. That is also written. The Chatuhshan were well established in Brahmananda and after getting the scent, aroma of the flowers and other things offered to the feet of Narayana, they gave up Brahmananda and started worshipping Narayana.

Sanatan Goswami when he was there in Maldah, Maldah was the capital at that time, Hussain Shah was the Emperor. He was there in one village called Ramakeli, I had been to that place, and Rupa Goswami and Anupam the younger brother, father of Jiva Goswami, after seeing Chaitanya Mahaprabhu they wanted to renounce the world, they did not want to remain in this world. Then Chaitanya Mahaprabhu said, “No, not now. When I shall go to Vrindavan then you can renounce.” After that when Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was travelling to Vrindavan, first Rupa Goswami with Anupam left that place. He was also a big person there with Hussain Shah Emperor. Sanatan Goswami was Prime Minister and our Rupa Goswami was finance minister, a big officer there. He left his position and renounced and after renouncing he met Chaitanya Mahaprabhu at Allahabad Prayag and he wrote to Sanatan Goswami to come immediately. He mentioned that Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is going Vrindavan. He is actually Guru, Rupa Goswami, Rupa Manjari and he is the dearest of him, so Sanatan Goswami has to carry out his order and what did he do? What is written in Chaitanya Charitamrita?

If anybody gets the grace of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, even a mean person gets His grace, they can become the introducer of Bhakti-shastra. He can initiate and write Bhakti sastra. It is the first verse, Kaviraja Goswami has written in twentieth chapter of Chaitanya Charitamrita.

Sanatan Goswami was jailed by Hussain Shah the King. When the King went to Orissa to conquer that region, he wanted to take Sanatan Goswami along. Sanatan Goswami was the Prime Minister and he did not want to go. He declined to go so he was sent to prison. At that time he got a letter from Rupa Goswami,

lines: na sad idaṁ jagad ity avadhāraya

blocks.text: “Where is Yadupate Krishna now? Where is His Mathura Dham? raghu-pateḥ kva gatottara-kośalā—where is Ayodhya Dham? And Ramachandra? Nothing is permanent in this world. Immediately come. Do not spoil a moment.”

When he had to carry out the orders of his Guru, Rupa Goswami being senior for that reason, Sanatan Goswami what did he do? He spoke to the jailor. The jailor was a Muslim and had offered him service. He spoke to him, “You are jindapir—you are a living saint.” He was not a living saint, but he said so.
“If you release one person from the prison then you will be released. You are jindapir.”
But the jailer was afraid, “No, I cannot do this. When the emperor comes he will kill me. I cannot do this.”
Speaking a lie is not good for a saint but for fulfilling the desire of Rupa Goswami and fulfilling the desire of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, he was ready to do anything.

lines: mannimittaṃ kṛtaṃ pāpam api dharmāya kalpate

blocks.text: The Lord says, “Even if someone does sinful activities for Me, they will be considered as righteous acts.”

Sanatan Goswami was ready to do anything for his satisfaction and he flattered him, spoke many things, excessively like, “You are a great saint” etc. The jailer was not ready to let him go. Then Sanatan Goswami said, “I gave you this job. I was Prime Minister at that time when I engaged you in this job. You should do something in return for me. I gave you some benefit and you should pay me that debt.”
That too a sadhu cannot demand. But here he said, “I have given you this service now you release me from this.”
“No, I cannot do this.”
“I shall give you five thousand gold coins, very valuable things.”
The jailer cannot think about this. To give a bribe is not a good thing, as a sadhu one should not do this. But he is doing it.
“Five thousand.”
“No. You will give me that but when the emperor comes he will kill me. So I cannot do this.”

Then he got about seven thousand gold coins and put them in his hand. There were ten thousand gold coins kept by Rupa Goswami for his release arrangement. By seeing them he the jailer got some sort of greediness to have them.
Then he said, “When Badshah will come to know he will hang me.”

“No, No, No. I shall not remain here, you take me out and say this half truth to him. You say, ‘I took him to Ganges for a bath and he jumped into the Ganges and went away.’ You should not think that I shall remain here. I shall take darveshvesh, I will become ascetic, Muslim ascetic darvesh. I will go to Mecca.”

They do not understand Vrindavan, so he said he will go to Mecca. “So there is no reason for you to be afraid.” Ultimately, he gave in. For fulfilling the desire of his Gurudev and Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, what he did, don’t you think! He did everything, it is not good to speak lie, but he did that.

He was released, he went through the villages, not through towns and cities, he is a well-known person and after a long time he came to Patraparvat, one mountain. There was a landowner there. In the day time he was a landowner and in the night time a robber. He has an astrologer and that astrologer told the robber landowner, “Sanatan Goswami has one person with him, Ishan, he has eight valuable gold coins. They thought they should kill them and take those. But Sanatan Goswami was very intelligent, he is not an ordinary person. He has a good grasp of Sanskrit, Arsi, Parsi and Hindi and is a very able man in Government. He was born into a Brahmin family, Bharadwaja family but he has no vanity and for that reason when Rupa Goswami and he were there with the King Hussain Shah tried to persuade him to remain there and continue as a Prime Minister. Sanatan Goswami replied, “No, I shall not go to the assembly. Whatever punishment you want to give you give.” Then he imprisoned him. The King has love for him. He knows that Sanatan Goswami is a very competent person and for that reason he needed him.

Now when Sanatan Goswami thought about the landowner who was helping him, serving him very much, “I am not known to him, he is liking me, he is showing me love so there is some reason behind that. Perhaps my servitor, Ishan has kept something with him.” He asked him, “Ishan, come here. Have you got anything with you?” Then he concealed one gold coin and showed seven gold coins. “Give them to me, why have you brought this? ‘Saṅge kene āniyācha ei kāla-yama’—why have you brought this, this is kāla-yama any moment we may be killed. Give me.” He took them and gave them to the landowner. He said, “Your Ishan has got eight gold coins and he has given seven gold coins only.”
“I do not want this.”
“We had the desire to kill you in the night. We do not want this money, you take the money we shall help you to cross the Ganges. I do not want money.”

Sanatan Goswami is very intelligent. He thought these people are now behaving and are very good but again they may become very bad. For that reason he gave all the gold coins to them. They then crossed the mountain and met Srikant, the husband of his sister. He wanted to take him to his own house.
“No, you have come so stay here for longer time.”
“No. I want to meet Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, He is residing in Braja Mandal. He is Krishna Himself.”

Then Srikant gave him a very costly rug, bhotkambal, taking that he came to Varanasi and sat outside the house of Chadrashekhar Vaidya. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu said to Chandrashekar Vaidya, “One Vaishnav has come outside. Bring him inside.” He came out and he saw a fakir.
“No, No there is a Muslim fakir.”
“Muslim fakir?”
“Yes”
“You call him.”
“Oh Fakir, our Mahaprabhu wants you”
And fakir went there.
When Sanatan Goswami entered in the house, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu ran and embraced him. Sanatan Goswami said, “I am very unholy, stop! You should not touch me.”
Mahaprabhu then said, “I touch you to purify My body in this way.”

After that he was asked by Mahaprabhu to become bhadra, become a gentleman, to shave his mustache etc as he had got beard. The beard and mustache were removed and after taking snan, a bath he came there. But what vastra (cloths), would he wear? He went to Chandrashekar. Chandrashekar gave him one new cloth. “No, I shall not take it.” Then he went to Tapan Mishra. He also brought one new cloth. “No, I want one used cloth, used by you.” Sanatan Goswami as personal associate of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is teaching us. I stay in this Math and if anybody give me used cloth, I do not take it. But here Sanatan Goswami has showed that you should take the remnants of Vaishnavas. From the life of Sanatan Goswami we are to learn so many teachings. There is no end to it. And after taking that used cloth he wore it but Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is seeing the very costly bhotkambal, the rug. This is not defeating, “You have got this sort of cloth?” Next day Sanatan Goswmai gave it to a babaji near Ganges, “Take this and give me your cloth.” He has got very bad cloth.
(Sanatan Goswami:) “Give it to me, I shall wear it.”
“You are joking with me.”
“No, no, I am not joking, grace me and give me your cloth.”

There were so many stitches in his garment. “You give me.” After exchanging Sanatan Goswami came to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Mahaprabhu was happy seeing the torn cloth. We belong to that group. He asked this question, ‘Who am I?’ to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu to teach the conditioned souls of this whole world. He is an emancipated soul. The first question should be this.
“Who am I? Why am I burning with the threefold afflictions? What is the object to be attained and what is the way to attain? I cannot even put a question to you. Please tell me everything.”

Then He started speaking. We have heard this when we entered into this Math sixty years before. But yet our Bhakti Siddhant Saraswati Goswami Thakur says, “You should repeatedly read, you have got no foundation. Only you say, you have got no belief. You should go through this, the foundation should be there. Without that if you build the structure, it will fall down.

Now what is the time? What can be done? There are so many things Sanatan Goswami has taught us. He had some scabies, itches, on his body while coming from Vrindavan. For that reason when Chaitanya Mahaprabhu used to embrace him, he would say, “Do not embrace me, I have got scabies, patra”. But He, Mahaprabhu,w repeatedly embraced him. Because of that he wanted to kill his body during Rathayatra. Then Chaitanya Mahaprabhu said to all the devotees what Sanatan Goswami was thinking, “His body is My body, he wants to finish it. He has got no right to do this. His body is My body like this.” He embraced him and all his itching, all sorts of scabies, disappeared.

articles.title: Guru Purnima
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: Srila Gurudev initially sings the glories of his most beloved Gurudev, remembering his extraordinary personality and how the impossible became possible just by the influence of his presence. He then sings the glories of Krishna Dvaipayan Vedvyas Muni and Sanatan Goswami and narrates important teachings from their lives.

blocks.text: There was a plan to go Agartala Math this year on Guru Purnima Tithi, but Krishna's wish was different so we could not go there. Our Gurudev brought his worshipable Supreme Lord to Agartala from Purushottam Dham. The deity you see there now was not there before. The deity which was there previously was broken by the children playing there. Those broken deities were being served there before but when our Gurudev went there, he instructed to the authorities there for not worshiping the broken deity. That time the king of that place, Krishnachandra Deva Bhattacharya requested Srila Gurudev to accept the service responsibility of that place. Srila Gurudev was not ready to accept that responsibility initially but on the repeated requests of the king he accepted the service. Guruji informed the king that the priest was not worshiping the deities in the proper way. He used to make offerings in the same plate on which he used to eat. Guruji told that if he was to take the responsibility then he will not be able to do it like that. So it is better to give responsibility of the temple to some other persons. But the king replied saying, “We do not know how to worship the deities according to the scriptures, so it is better you take the responsibility of the temple and the deities”. Prior to this, when Srila Gurudev visited the king's house to meet him for the first time, the king was impressed to see the extraordinary personality of Srila Gurudev. He never had Darshan of any Mahapurush like Srila Gurudev before.
In his speech he mentioned, “Just by having Darshan of your Gurudev, I have decided that I will give responsibility of the temple to him only. Only he is the eligible person for that.”

Though, Srila Gurudev did not ask for the temple service, Lord Jagannath chose him for His service. Guruji's personality was not ordinary. Even in Chandigarh, the Government officers were not ready to give the land where our Math was established later. The land was a part of a public garden. They requested Guruji to choose other land for the Math but he liked that land only. That time one IPS officer who was very intelligent asked us, “You have to answer our questions and satisfy many persons here to get that land.” That time one advocate also had gone with us. The officer asked us many questions like; why do you want that land? Whom do you worship there? What benefit would you get? He then refuted all the answers we gave him. Our conversation continued for about one hour or so and in that all the time he opposed us. We thought we would not get that land. But at the end the decision came in our favor! What had happened? That was because of our Guru Maharaj.

In Puri also, all, even ISKCON ran away, they could not get possession of Prabhupad's birth place. Everyone had their faith in Guruji only. Guruji was like that. He never leaves any task incomplete. In Puri, I told him, “There are so many difficulties for you here. There are no proper arrangements for you to stay. You are having sleepless nights. I request you to quit the efforts of getting this place.”

Srila Gurudev did not pay even a little attention to my proposal and asked me to write a letter to the respective authority. I met devotees of other Maths like Chaitanya Math etc, they said they do not have any interest in getting that place but when Srila Gurudev decided to get it, they tried to trouble him. Gangadar Mahapatro told us that by giving some proofs they were trying to prove that their Math is the original Math. So Srila Gurudev had to face so many hurdles while getting the appearance place of Srila Prabhupad. It was almost impossible to get that place. Guru Maharaj sent us a message, “We are busy in Amritsar, you do whatever you want.”
I replied, “We cannot do anything. Governor, ministers all are in their pockets.”
Later Guruji came there. That time we were in Srila Santa Goswami Maharaj's Math. He asked me, “Do we have an appointment with the Governor?”
I replied, “No, we do not have any appointment.”

Later without any appointment we went to the Governor's house. The Governor was going out that time in his car with so many other cars and police officers following him. Guru Maharaj got down from his car. When the Governor saw Guru Maharaj, he stopped his car, came out and offered his obeisances to him. His personality was like that! You would have never seen a person like him!
Guru Maharaj told him, “I have come to see you.”
He replied, “Yes, yes. I am coming back soon. Do not worry. Please wait, I will come back in a short time.”

He came back after some time. After seeing and listening to Guru Maharaj, he was impressed. The opposite party's pocket became empty, everything came out. Srila Gurudev had such an extraordinary personality! You would never find such a personality anywhere else! He was also very expert in dealing with people. Seeing his personality, everyone used to surrender to him.

In Agartala, in Chakdah, everywhere, it had happened so. They forcefully gave their temple's service to Gurudev. In Chakdah, the temple authority wanted to give responsibility of the temple to Guruji. He told them that he can speak Harikatha for a few days there as it is Jagannath Deva's place. He also gave some money for the maintenance of the service. They had sold their land etc. to maintain the temple service. They only had a small ground for the bathing ceremony. They again and again requested Guruji to take the responsibility of the temple. Then Guruji thought, “May be Jagannath wants to give His service to us.” We told Guruji that if we take responsibility of that temple then we will have to spend so much money on renovation and maintenance of the temple. But Guruji accepted that responsibility happily. Like that in Puri also, although we got Prabhupad's birthplace, it was a very old house which required full renovation and construction. (This was after the disappearance of Srila Paramgurudev) We were worried about how to accomplish such a big service responsibility.

One day Srila Krishnadas Babaji Maharaj, Pujyapad Keshava Prabhu and I were going to some place in Puri and that time a car came and suddenly stopped on the road. A person came out from the car and offered five hundred rupees to me as a donation. We had never seen him before. We did not know him. Why has he given money? We asked him his name and some information about him. He was Singhaniya. (Who later helped in the construction of Puri temple by monitory service) Actually, Guruji gave us an indication, “You go to that person; your task would be accomplished.” Whatever happens, even when not in his direct presence, happens by his will only.

Here in Kolkata something similar happened on Srila Gurudev's disappearance day. There were so many devotees gathered for the celebration. I asked the Math in-charge about what things will be there in Prasadam. He replied there would be potato curry. I thought, ‘Guruji used to like Dhoka-sabji (a curry prepared from chickpeas lentils). But it was difficult to prepare it for so many people. There were not enough funds for that.’ Long back on one occasion, I inquired to Srila Gurudev whether to have Paneer curry in Prasadam at the time of celebration, he responded by saying, “Preparing Dhoka will be best.” So we prepared Dhoka. Gurumaharaj used to like it. But that year, on the disappearance day of Srila Gurudev, the Math in-charge told me, “We do not have enough funds and time to prepare Dhoka”. I was disappointed. But suddenly one person came, I had not seen him before and also never saw him after that. He gave me five thousand rupees. I was astonished! I had never seen him before and he is giving five thousand rupees in donation. I felt Guruji has sent him to us. Immediately I informed the Math in-charge to prepare Dhoka; whatever money is required he could take from me. We can only desire to do something, he is always behind us. He can make it happen.
Today is Guru-purnima Tithi. Krishna Dvaipayan Vedavyas Muni is Guru of all. Daily we sing,

lines: nārada haite vyās, madhva kahe vyās-dāsa,

blocks.text: Sri Krishna is the original Guru, from Him the Parampara (disciplic succession) starts. Our Gurudev comes in the same Parampara. From Gurudev, gradually it goes up to Lord Sri Krishna.

Today is the appearance day of Krishna Dvaipayan Vedavyas Muni. How did he appear? One day, Parashar Muni, a very powerful personality, wanted to cross a river but as all the boatmen were busy that time, one fisherman asked his daughter, Satyavati to drive the boat and help the Muni to cross the river. Parashar Muni became very much pleased with her. As she was Matsya-gandha, the smell of fish was coming out from her body. Parashar Muni became merciful on her and with his power he changed her to Padma-ganda. So nice fragrance of flowers started coming out from her body. And by Parashar Muni, Vedavyas Muni was born in the womb of Satyavati. (This was the arrangement by which the great personality like Vedavyas Muni had to come to this world so Parashar Muni had enacted the pastime of being attracted by Satyavati.) Immediately after his birth, Vedavyas Muni told his mother, “Mother, I am going with my father. But whenever you will remember me, I shall be present in front of you,” Have you ever heard any child speak like this immediately after his birth? What do you understand by that? Is Vedavyas Muni an ordinary man?

When Lord Kapila Deva was in the womb of his mother Devahuti, demigods offered their prayers to her womb at Bindu Sarovar. After He came out from her womb she inquired from Him, “Because of my lusty desires, I wished to have a son.”
Lord Kapila Deva smiled and replied, “If you had lusty desires, the Lord would not have appeared in your womb.”
It is said, ‘janha kam tanha nahi ram’—the Lord will not appear at the place where there exists a desire for material things.

Kapila Deva told, “You and your husband, performed severe penance and by your devotion you have got Me. There is not even a tinge of lusty desire in you. Your heart is pure but for the welfare of the conditioned souls you had got that desire and for them only, you are asking this question.”

The appearance pastime of Krishna Dvaipayan Vedavyas Muni is beyond our comprehension. He appeared on an island. In Sanskrit, an island is called Dvipa. And as his complexion was black (Krishna), he is called Krishna Dvaipayan. He divided the Vedas into four.

His mother, Satyavati, later got married to Shantanu and had two sons, Vichitra Virya and Chitrangada. Chitrangada was killed in a battle. Bhisma Deva, the brother of Vichitra Virya who accepted Shantanu and Ganga Devi as his parents, kidnapped two princesses to get married to Vichitra Virya. But Vichitra Virya fell ill of consumption and died childless. Satyavati then got worried thinking who would continue her progeny as Bhisma Deva had decided not to marry. She remembered her son Vedavyas Muni and he immediately appeared there. Satyavati told him about her distress. So from Vedavyas Muni, Dritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura were born. Dhritarashtra was blind but was very powerful. He had a hundred sons. Vidura was a the son of a maid, but he was a great devotee of the Lord.

Vedavyas Muni gave special powers to Sanjay with which he narrated whatever happened at Kurukshetra to Dhritarashtra being at the palace itself. Can any ordinary person give such power to anybody? Was he an ordinary man? Millions of people died in the Kurukshetra battle. Seeing the plight of all the females lamenting for their husbands, Vedavyas Muni, with his special power, showed them their husbands. Seeing their husbands they were all satisfied.

When he was at Badrikashram, a desire of writing the scriptures came into his heart. He approached Ganesh to help him write whatever was revealed to him. He would speak and Ganesh would write. Ganesh had one condition, that while he is writing he should not stop at anytime. Vedavyas Muni agreed to it and in return he also put one condition; whatever he writes he must understand the meaning of it. Vedavyas Muni started speaking, in between he used to speak some verses to understand the meaning of which Ganesh had to realise. An ordinary man cannot have such power. The Supreme Lord Himself empowered him with His energy. Those who had been to Badrinath, they know that at about a thousand feet above the Badrinarayan temple there situated the Vyasdev cave. Once I had been to that place with Guruji. The mountain where his cave is looks like a Granth (book). Vedavyas Muni wrote scriptures pertaining to dharm, artha, kama for different classes of people in the society who are entangled in bodily conception. Those who want wealth, for them he wrote artha-shastra, for those who want to fulfill their material desires he wrote kama-shastra and those who want to enjoy the heavenly planets after death for them he wrote appropriate scriptures. Even after writing so many scriptures he performed a pastime of not getting peace or satisfaction in his heart. He wrote about liberation or salvation also but still he was not at peace. He was not an ordinary man.

He remembered his revered Gurudev, Narad Rishi. Narad Rishi appeared there at Badrinarayan. We sing, 'nārada haite vyās'—in disciplic succession the knowledge came to Vyasdev from Narad Rishi. When Narad Rishi appeared, Vyasdev offered his obeisance to him and asked for his grace.
Narad Rishi asked him, “Is your soul, entangled to a material and subtle body, at peace?”

He replied, “You are antaryami (knower of everyone's heart). I have written so many scriptures. I gave everything to fulfill the desire of different classes of people. Those who wanted wealth, for them I wrote artha-shastra, those who wanted to fulfill their material desires, for them I wrote kama-shastra and those who wanted to enjoy the heavenly planets after death, for them I wrote appropriate scriptures, so why have I not got peace?”
Narad Rishi replied, “You have done abominable work; whatever you have given is non-eternal and perishable. You have given more miseries to them. How could you expect to get peace?”
“I have written about salvation also.”

“It is even more abominable. You have completely closed the path for them to reach the Supreme Lord. The Supreme Lord is the personification of peace, He is purna-sat (eternal), purna-cit (full of knowledge) and purna-anand (full of bliss). He is purna-saccidanand. Your writing should be for the satisfaction of the Supreme Lord. Have you sung His glories?”
“Yes, I have written in Mahabharat”

“No, it will not work, you have to write for His satisfaction. In Mahabharat, you have written about devotion to Him while writing Gita but it is without sharanagati (surrender). It cannot reach there. You will get sharanagati by His grace only.”
Bhaktivinoda Thakur has written in his sharanagati hymns,

lines: kāńdiyā kāńdiyā bale āmi to’ adhama

blocks.text: Only by the grace of a surrendered soul, do you get sharanagati. Sharanagati is the eternal nature of the soul. For whomever the eternal nature, Divine Love for the Supreme Lord, is awakened, he is a surrendered soul. Pray for sharanagati from the core of the heart. One should have humility (dainya); should not have any material ego. The next is atma-nivedan—I am of Krishna, not of this material world. Only Krishna is my maintainer and sustainer. Mahaprabhu Himself says in Sikshashtakam, “You always blame the Supreme Lord and His devotees (that you are not getting Him). Do you want Him from the core of your heart? If you really want Him then you will get Him at that very moment. But you do not want Him.”
From the core of your heart you say,

lines: na dhanaṁ na janaṁ na sundarīṁ

blocks.text: Speak from your heart, “I do not want wealth.”
Outside we speak but inside we think, without wealth how will I be able to sustain in this world? We fear from inside. Many persons come here in Gaudiya Math or visit some temple.
Some person thinks, “If by visiting temple, I would able to make my daughter marry then I will come daily.”
Some think, “I want five lakhs rupees for my daughter's marriage. I offer a thousand rupees; please arrange five lakh rupees for me.”
If he does not get five lakhs rupees then he will say, “I will never visit this temple again.”
Why did he come? From core of your heart, you have to say, “I do not want wealth.”

Everyone in this material world is running after money. The Supreme Lord will say, “If you want wealth, then why should I come to you? Whatever wants you have in your heart, I would give you that only. I am sitting in your heart”
“O Arjuna! The Lord is situated in the hearts of everyone and is directing the wandering of all living entities, who are seated on a machine, made of the material energy.”

It is not possible to cheat Him. Speak from core of your heart, “I do not want wealth.” You speak very firmly. Who is the giver of the wealth, He is Krishna only. (If you do not depend on Him for your maintenance). Is it sharanagati?
We say, “I do not want a wife, daughter or son.”

We are merely speaking from the mouth not from the heart. Can we say, “I do not want any scholarship or liberation, I only want your causeless devotion?” The Lord will say, “You ask for Me and I will be there at that very moment.” If He could grace Gajendra, an animal, then why not us? But we do not want Him from the core of our heart. We are from Krishna, in Krishna, by Krishna and for Krishna. No one is there for us other than Krishna. He is our sole protector and maintainer. He would protect us from the enemies outside as well as the enemies inside us. We should accept whatever is favorable to the devotion to Lord and give up whatever is not favorable to devotion. It is very difficult to find a pure devotee of the Lord. It is very, very rare.

Narad Rishi gave Chatu-shloki-bhagavat—the four Shloka of Bhagavat to Vedvyas Muni. In Srimad Bhagavatam, importance is given to the word, 'aham' meaning 'I' (It is used to represent the Supreme). He says, “The eternal and non-eternal (sad-asad), everything, exists because of Me only. I exist before the manifestation of this world and I will be there after annihilation also.”

Everyone has to die (will leave their body) one day. In Gujarat, there was an earthquake, millions of people died in it; the Supreme Lord was witnessing it. He is neutral. They understood that they had died. In reality, there is no birth, there is no death.
Sri Krishna says in Gita,
“This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross over it.”

Take shelter of the Supreme Lord like that which Gajendra took. Immediately he saw that there is nothing like birth or death. It is all illusion. The soul neither has birth nor death. He is eternal. He will never die. If he stays for the Supreme Lord whose energy’s expansion he is, only then will he become happy. He is from Him, by Him and for Him. Therefore it is said that associate with pure devotees. They will give that real knowledge and will enlighten the eternal nature of the soul.

Iswara Puri and Ramachadra Puri both were in the service of Madhavedra Puripad. When Madhavedra Puripad was crying out of separation pangs from Krishna, Ramchadra Puri tried to console him advising him to become absorbed in Brahman. Madhavedra Puripad got angry with him and thought, “I wanted to engage him in the service but he is giving me pain by advising about Brahman conception. He does not know the ontological aspect of the Supreme Lord (Bhagavat-tatva).” People with such ideology recite ‘soham’—I am that Absolute and ‘aham brahmasmi’—I am that Absolute Brahman. They also perform Vyasa-puja or Guru-puja on Guru-purnima. They also serve Guru. But that service is not the same as the service done by devotees of the Lord. Their service is not real service. They consider themselves to be non-different from the Lord. How will service be possible with that conception?

Therefore, Narad Goswami advises Vyasdev to write the Bhagavatam for the satisfaction of the Supreme Lord. If He will be satisfied, you will be satisfied and everyone will be satisfied. When we had gone to Punjab, with Guruji, a group of people who believed in the Brahman conception once invited Gurudev to their place. When they heard Srila Gurudev speak Harikatha, they were afraid thinking, “If we invite him again then our ideology of ‘soham’—I am Bhagavan, will get defeated.” So they did not invite him again. But what had happened there? The whole Punjab became devotees. Who is a real Guru? Our Guruji is the real Guru.

There is one more cult, the Arya-samaji, who considers the transcendental form of the Lord, the deity (Vigrah) as an idol, matter. There is one per person in Hyderabad who is the main follower of this ideology, Dayanand Sarasvati. He has written commentary on Vedvyas Muni’s writings. I have seen his picture in Hoshiyarpur, Punjab. There was some dispute occurred there. We were in Hoshiyarpur that time. There the followers of Arya-samaj ideology have kept one idol of Dayanand Sarasvati in his memory. One person who was a judge in the high court asked them, “If you consider the idol of any person as matter, could you hit this idol with your feet?” A person from that ideology said we do not believe his idol as a person and hit it with his feet. Many of his followers protested such an act. The protestors said, “You hit the person who has established this organization with your feet!” Why did they feel so? Because the idol represents the person himself.

Narad Goswami advised Vyasdev Muni to first become absorbed in the transcendental form of the Supreme Lord and then write Bhagavatam. And after writing Bhagavatam, Vyasdev Muni got eternal bliss. Sukadeva Goswami, the son of Vyasdev Muni recited Bhagavatam at Sukratal for Pariksit Maharaj. Sukadeva Goswami was Brahma-gyani right from his birth itself. He left his parents as soon as he came out from his mother’s womb. Vyasdev Muni performed pastimes of separation and grief from him and ran behind him to get him back. He called out, “O my son! O my son!” Internally, he was not lamenting.

Pariksit Maharaj was cursed by a Brahmin that he will die after seven days by the bite of a snake-bird, ‘Takshak’. He renounced everything and went to the forest. All the Rishi-munis advised him to follow different paths like karma, gyan, yoga etc. Pariksit Maharaj was bewildered on which path to follow so he remembered Krishna for help and Krishna sent Sukadeva Goswami to him. When Sukadeva Goswami came to that place, naked, all the Rishi-munis, Parasuram etc. stood up.
Sukadeva Goswami heard Srimad Bhagavatam from Vyasdev at Badrinarayan. There was one speaker and one listener. It was so silent that you could hear a pin drop.

The place where Sukadeva Goswami came, there were lakhs of persons assembled including Rishi-munis and many kings. Sukadeva Goswami said, “You will have to listen to Bhagavatam. No need to do anything. I am saying this. I was established in Brahmanand. The narration of Srimad Bhagavatam attracted me. For seven days you will have to listen to Bhagavatam incessantly.”

We will not come to Math the next day if someone tells us like that. Sukadeva Goswami, in between, asked Pariksit Maharaj to drink water and to eat something. But Pariksit Maharaj said, “You do not worry about me. You are making me drink the nectar, so I do not want to eat or drink anything.”

Pariksit Maharaj got the highest attainment just by listening to Harikatha incessantly for seven days and seven nights. Prahlad Maharaj got the highest attainment by remembering the Supreme Lord. So it is said in Chaitanya Charitamrita,
“When one is firmly fixed in devotion then whether he executes one form of devotion or many, the waves of love for the Supreme Lord gets awakened in him.”

So one must perform Guru-puja on Guru-purnima Tithi. It is the full-moon day of the month Ashadh (Hindu calendar month). We pray for the grace of Sukadeva Goswami and Vyasdev Muni. Vyasdev Muni is non-different from the Supreme Lord. He enacted the pastimes and experienced the highest bliss. Our Gurudev read Bhagavatam for about an hour at that place (Badrinarayan).
Srila Srinath Chakravarti has expressed the essence of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s teachings in one verse,

lines: ramyā kācid upāsanā vraja-vadhū-vargeṇā yā kalpitā

blocks.text: “According to Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, we are to worship Vrajesh-tanaya—the son of Nanda Maharaj. His transcendental abode is at Vrindavan. The mode of worship of Gopis is the best—madhurya-rasa (conjugal love). The evidence of this is there in Srimad Bhagavatam. And the highest objective, the highest end of life is Krishna-prema—Divine Love.”
If we have taken the shelter of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu then we have to follow His teachings as it is. It is not good to deviate a bit from it. We should take absolute shelter of Srimad Bhagavatam.

Today is also the disappearance day of Sanatan Goswami. He is also our Guru. In a worldly sense, Rupa Goswami is the younger brother of him but in reality Sanatan Goswami is serving under Rupa Goswami. They have worked with the emperor, Husain Shah and have come from South India; they come in the dynasty of Sarvakya Muni. They were six brothers. Amongst six of them, the mention of Sanatan Goswami, Rupa Goswami and Anupam Mallik comes in Chaitanya Charitamrita. Sanatan Goswami’s name was Sakar Mallik, Rupa Goswami was Dabir Khas. Anupam Mallik is the father of Jiva Goswami.
They recieved Darshan of Mahaprabhu in Maladah. There were lakhs of devotees with Mahaprabhu that time. He was travelling to Vrindavan. That time Sanatan Goswami told Him,

lines: yāṅra saṅge haya ei loka lakṣa koṭi

blocks.text: “One should not go Vrindavan with so many people.”

On the way there are many places ruled by Muslim emperors. So Sanatan Goswami indicated to the Lord not to go to Vrindavan with so many people. Mahaprabhu then came back from Kanayi Natashala and returned to Nilachal Dham.

Then later, Mahaprabhu again started for Vrindavan, first Rupa Goswami and Anupam left their duties and went there to have His Darshan. Rupa Goswami also informed Sanatan Goswami by writing a letter in a secret language so that others do not understand the meaning of it. He wrote, “Where is Ayodhya Dham? Where is Krishna’s Mathura Puri? Nothing is permanent in this world.”

Sanatan Goswami understood the meaning of it and left his duties as Prime Minister and started reading scriptures while at his residence. He informed the King that his health is not good. He was very dear to the King. The King visited him at his place and came to know about his mood. He tried to persuade him profusely but Sanatan Goswami told, “I want to read scriptures. I do not have interest in continuing my duty.”
The King replied, “I am going to Orissa for war.”
Sanatan Goswami replied, “You are going to give pain to Jagannath Deva’s servant. I will not go with you.”

The King then imprisoned him. Sanatan Goswami was subservient to Rupa Goswami and he was ordered by him to come to associate with Mahaprabhu. So to be rescued from the jail, Sanatan Goswami tried to persuade the jailer, “I helped you getting the job, now if you release me then Khuda (Muslim calls God with this name) will be satisfied with you.”

The jailer refused to do this because he was fearful of the King. Sanatan Goswami tried to allure him by giving him assurance of giving five thousand gold coins. Rupa Goswami had put ten thousand gold coins for Sanatan Goswami to help him get rescued from the King. The jailer told that if he would release him then the King will kill him. At which Sanatan Goswami told, “The King has gone for the battle so there is no surety that he will come back. Even if he comes, you can tell him that you took me out for my daily morning routine activities and there I jumped in the River Ganga. I am not going to come back. I will go to Mecca (Vrindavan). So you do not worry.”

After listening this also the jailer was afraid and was not ready to release him. Then Sanatan Goswami brought seven thousand gold coins and put in front of him. The jailer had never seen so many gold coins even in his dreams. So his mind changed and he released Sanatan Goswami. Sanatan Goswami along with one devotee, Ishan, crossed the river and started his journey to meet Mahaprabhu towards Vrindavan. He renounced everything, wealth, position, followers. They then reached to Patra Mountain. There was one landlord who used to do robbery in the night. They became guest to him. He had one astrologer with him who told that the servant of Sanatan Goswami has eight gold coins with him. So he was showing overt affection and respect to them. Sanatan Goswami was very intelligent and he understood that there is something wrong as he is showing too much affection towards them.
He called Ishan and asked him, “Do you have anything with you?”
He said he has seven gold coins with him.
Sanatan Goswami told him, “Give me, why have you brought this?” It comes in Chaitanya Charitamrita Madhya 20.25,
Sanatan Goswami chastised Ishan, saying, “Why have you brought this death knell (kāla-yama) with you?” He took them and gave them to the landowner.

The landowner told, “Your Ishan has got eight gold coins and he has given seven only. I had decided to kill you tonight but as you are giving these seven gold coins without even asking, I have become happy so I will not take these coins from you. You keep them with you, we shall help you to cross the mountain without taking anything from you.”
It comes in the scripture,

How can one have faith in the words of a rascal? He sometimes tells the truth and sometimes falsehoods. Just as with the clouds of month of Shravan (Indian calendar month), sometimes there is sunshine and sometimes it rains.
So Sanatan Goswami told the landlord that they do not want his favor without paying for it. Better he takes the seven gold coins to make them cross the mountain. They thus crossed the mountain.

After crossing the mountain, he asked Ishan whether he has any gold coin with him. He said he had one. Then he asked him, “Will this coin protect you? You have come with me thinking like this. Keep that coin with you and return back.”
Srila Prabhupad has written in his ‘vaishnava ke’ kirtan,

lines: śikṣā dila yāhā, cinta sei saba

blocks.text: Here, Srila Prabhupad has not cited any incident from Bhagavatam or Chaitanya Charitamrita, he has advised us to go through the teachings given to Sanatan Goswami by Mahaprabhu with utmost care.

After crossing the mountain, Sanatan Goswami met Srikant, the husband of his sister. He gifted him one costly rug, a Bhotkambal, taking which he came to Varanasi and sat outside the house of Chandra Shekhar Vaidya. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu said to Chandra Shekar Vaidya, “One Vaishnava has come outside. You please bring him inside.” Chandra Shekhar came out and saw a fakir there.
He then said to Mahaprabhu, “There is no Vaishnav outside. There is one Muslim fakir standing there.”
Mahaprabhu: “Muslim fakir?”
“Yes”
“You call him.”
“O Fakir, our Mahaprabhu wants to meet you.”
And the fakir went inside.
When Sanatan Goswami entered in the house, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu ran and embraced him. Sanatan Goswami told, “I am very unholy. You please stop. You should not touch me.”
Mahaprabhu, “I touch you to purify My body in this way.”

After that he was asked by Mahaprbhu to dress up like a gentleman. Sanatan Goswami then did so and after taking bath he came back there. Now, what cloths would he wear? Chandra Shekhar Acharya offered him with one new cloth in response to which he said, “No, I shall not take new cloths.” Then he went to Tapan Mishra. He also brought one new cloth. “No, I want one used cloth; used by you.”

Sanatan Goswami as personal associate of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is teaching us. I stay in this Math and if anybody gives me used cloth, I do not take it. But here Sanatan Goswami has showed that you should take the remnants of Vaishnavas. From the life of Sanatan Goswami we are to learn so many teachings. There is no end of it. After taking that used cloth he wore them up and came to Mahaprabhu again. He had the costly Bhotkambal, the rug with him. Mahaprabhu is seeing that rug wore by him. Sanatan Goswami understood that Mahaprabhu disliked that costly rug he had. The next day, he gave it to a Babaji near Ganges, “Take this and give me your cloth.” He has got very bad cloth.
(Sanatan Goswami:) “Give it to me, I shall wear it.”
“You are joking with me.”
“No, no, I am not joking, grace me and give me your cloth.”

There were so many stitches in his garment. “You give me.” (After exchanging) Sanatan Goswami came to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Mahaprabhu was happy seeing that (the torn cloth). We belong to that group.
He asked a question, “Who am I?” to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu to teach the conditioned souls of this whole world. He is an emancipated soul.

We should first ask these questions, 'ke āmi', 'kene āmāya jāre tāpa-traya' ihā nāhi jāni--'kemane hita haya' “Who am I? Why am I burning with the threefold affliction? What is the object to be attained and what is the way to attain it?”
He says, “I cannot even put questions to you. You please tell me everything.”

Then Mahaprabhu started speaking; we have heard this when we entered into this Math sixty years before. But yet our Bhakti Siddhant Saraswati Goswami Thakur says, “You should repeatedly read, you have got no foundation. Only you say, you have got no belief. You should go through this, foundation should be there. Without that if you build the structure, it will fall down.”

There are so many things Sanatan Goswami has taught us. He had some scabies on his body while coming from Vrindavan. For that reason when Chaitanya Mahaprabhu used to embrace him, he would say, “Please do not embrace me, I have got scabies”. But Mahaprabhu repeatedly embraced him. Because of that he wanted to kill his body during Rathayatra. Then Chaitanya Mahaprabhu said to all the devotees what Sanatan Goswami was thinking, “His body is Mine and he wants to finish it. He has got no right to do so. His body belongs to Me.” He embraced him and by that all the scabies on his body disappeared.

articles.title: Manifestations of Guru
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaja
articles.excerpt: Disciples perform gurupūja by singing the glories of Gurudeva, I perform gurupūja by hearing. But by hearing the glories, if I have got the evil motive of misappropriating it, it will not be gurupūja. As chanting is bhakti, hearing is also bhakti. In whatever way devotees may express their hearts, they are all my objects of worship.

blocks.text: The following is an extract from the sermon delivered by His Divine Grace Om Vishnupad 108 Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Dayita Mādhav Goswāmi Mahārāj, Founder of Śrī Chaitanya Gauḍīya Maṭh (Regd.) on the holy day of his advent on Śrī Utthān Ekādaśi Tithi in 1967 at Śrī Chaitanya Gauḍīya Maṭh, 35, Satish Mukherjee Road, Calcutta-26 :-
To me Gurudeva manifests himself in four forms, viz :-

gu + ru—one who destroys ignorance. Appearance of the Absolute Knowledge, Bhagavān, removes ignorance. Hence, original guru is Bhagavān.

He who has engaged me in the service of Bhagavān directly is the second appearance of my Śrīla Gurudeva—Most Revered Nityalīlapraviṣṭa Prabhupād Śrīmad Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswati Goswāmi Ṭhākur, Founder of the world-wide Śrī Chaitanya Maṭh and Śrī Gauḍīya Maṭh organisations.

Vaiṣṇavas are the third appearance of Gurudeva. What do they do? As Gurudeva always engages his disciples in the service of his object of worship, vaiṣṇavas also do the same.

Disciples are the fourth manifestation of guru. They, as disciples, actually do the work of a guru, i.e. they engage me always in the service of Gurudeva. There is no scope of doing any anti-devotional act of violation. If there is any violation, they will detect it. Hence, disciples are also my Guruvarga. Disciples perform gurupūja by singing the glories of Gurudeva, I perform gurupūja by hearing. But by hearing the glories, if I have got the evil motive of misappropriating it, it will not be gurupūja. As chanting is bhakti, hearing is also bhakti. In whatever way devotees may express their hearts, they are all my objects of worship.

articles.title: Characteristics of Bona Fide Guru
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: Śrī Viśwanāth Chakravarty Ṭhākur, in his commentary, has given a clue to the bona fide neophyte aspirants to recognize guru by one external quality—a bona fide guru is not subdued by passions— anger, greed etc. Of course, a realized soul can use the passions for the service of the Supreme Lord and for the eternal benefit of conditioned souls, but he can never be subjugated by them.

blocks.text: Refrain from various thoughts of this world, rise up, and reinstate your actual self by giving up all non-eternal desires. Sincerely endeavor to realize God by the grace of saintly persons (realized souls). This world is like a sharp razor and very difficult to cross over. There is no way to get deliverance from worldly bondage without taking absolute shelter of a bona fide Guru to worship God. This is the advice of realized souls. As a diseased person cannot treat himself, he has to take the help of an experienced doctor. The doctor, after examination, will diagnose the disease and prescribe medicine and appropriate diet. If the diagnosis is correct, the patient will recover from the disease. Similarly, the malady of births and deaths and threefold afflictions cannot be removed by human efforts. It is essential to take shelter of a bona fide guru—bona fide spiritual doctor. An experienced doctor is capable of treating the patient but a doctor in name, without experience, cannot treat the patient. So-called gurus, so-called sādhus, cannot have the capacity to treat the disease of enslaved jīvas—embodied souls.

Mahādeva's instruction to Pārvati—‘There may be many so-called gurus in this world to squeeze money from disciples, but a bona fide guru who can remove the drawbacks and sufferings of disciples is very rare.’

If we want quality, we cannot get quantity. If we are keen to increase quantity, we shall have to sacrifice quality. Who is a bona fide guru? What are the characteristics of a bona fide guru? Prabuddha Muni's instructions in regard to this ––

‘Therefore, enquire from Gurudeva about the best eternal welfare with complete submission to him. A bona fide guru is endowed with two special qualities : 1) He is well-versed in authentic scriptures and 2) has realization of Divinity.’

Śrīla Viśwanāth Chakravarty, in his commentary to this verse, explained the characteristics of a bona fide guru . Gurudeva should be well-versed in the Vedas and other allied scriptures. An aspirant disciple cannot progress in his worship of God without taking shelter of a truly qualified bona fide guru, who should have the capacity of removing the doubts of disciples by reasoning substantiated with evidence from authentic scriptures. If Gurudeva is incapable of removing the doubts of the disciple, the disciple's belief in him may slacken. The second characteristic of Gurudeva is that he should have realization of the divinity. Only by theoretical knowledge of the scriptures, without having practical realization, the spiritual guide cannot give proper advice and direction in accordance with the eligibility of the disciple. By the instruction of a guru, possessing the quality of practical realization, the disciple can have actual spiritual progress. It is to be considered here that a disciple can have the capacity to comprehend scriptural knowledge of Gurudeva by hearing from him; but how can a disciple understand whether Gurudeva has got realization of divinity or not? The Supreme Lord is transcendental reality; His absolute counterpart Gurudeva is also transcendental. Therefore, a neophyte votary cannot understand Gurudeva's realization of divinity by his own endeavor.

There are two aspects of the Supreme Lord and His absolute counterpart Gurudeva—(1) morphological aspect and (2) ontological aspect. Conditioned souls can, by their mind, intellect and sense-organs, grasp the morphological, i.e. the external aspect of the thing—the thing as it appears—but not the thing as it is. The thing as it is can be realized only by the grace of transcendental realities, through unconditional complete surrender. As for example the self-luminous sun can only be known by its own light and not by the help of other lights. We cannot see the sun in the night with the help of other lights, but when the sun rises, by accepting the grace of the sun—its light—we can see the sun and all things of this world in the proper perspective. The Supreme Lord and His Absolute Counterpart Gurudeva are self-effulgent. Śrī Viśwanāth Chakravarty Ṭhākur, in his commentary, has given a clue to the bona fide neophyte aspirants to recognize guru by one external quality—a bona fide guru is not subdued by passions— anger, greed etc. Of course, a realized soul can use the passions for the service of the Supreme Lord and for the eternal benefit of conditioned souls, but he can never be subjugated by them. Śrī Narottam Ṭhākur has advised us how the cardinal passions, except for malice, can be used for the service of Śrī Krishna—

lines: kāma Krishna karmārpaṇe, krodha bhakta-dveśi jane

blocks.text: Kāma—passion for fulfillment of desires should be diverted towards desire to serve Śrī Krishna, 'anger' should be used against those who are hostile to devotees, 'greed' should be employed to increase the desire to hear Hari katha from a bona fide sādhu, “infatuation” should be about not being able to utilise the valuable time of this precious human birth for worship of Śrī Krishna up till now and “madness” should be after singing the glories of Śrī Krishna. Even Nārada Goswāmi, out of compassion, used anger on the sons of Kuber—Nalkuber and Maṇigriva—to rescue them. According to the Gītā, the cause of anger is obstruction to fulfillment of one's desire. A real devotee cannot have any desire of his own except service of Śrī Krishna. So, in a pure devotee, there cannot be any possibility of the origination of such anger due to hindrance to worldly desires.
It is essential for the votary to submit to Gurudeva wholeheartedly with words, mind, sense-organs and everything for realization of divinity. Evidence from Muṇḍaka Śṛti:-

‘A brāhmin should have the knowledge that the fruits of karma are non-eternal and that eternal reality cannot be attained by karma. As such a brāhmin has no attachment to karma and therefore he takes absolute shelter at the lotus feet of a bona fide guru.’

Two characteristics of a bona fide guru are mentioned in Muṇḍaka Śṛti— “śrotriyaṁ” and “brahma-niṣṭham”. Interpretations of the word śrotriyaṁ : (1) Well-versed in śṛti sāstras—the Vedas and other allied scriptures and (2) blessed by the descent of the Divine knowledge through preceptorial channel. brahma-niṣṭham means firmly fixed in Brahman.

articles.title: Follow the Mahajanas
articles.author: Sreela Bhaktivinoda Thakura
articles.excerpt: Chanting the holy name of Krishna is the path of devotional service exhibited by the previous mahajanas. A path cannot be manufactured. Whatever path is there should be accepted by sadhus. Those who are proud and want fame try vigorously to discover new paths. Those who have good fortune from past lives give up pride and respect the established path. Those who are unfortunate promenade on a new path and thus cheat the world.

blocks.text: Aspiring devotees should first take shelter of the lotus feet of a bona fide guru. Without taking shelter of a guru, one cannot achieve anything auspicious. There are two types of people-one has developed intelligence and one has undeveloped intelligence. Those whose intelligence is undeveloped are absorbed in the so-called happiness of this world. If by chance they get the association of a mahajana, then they also become intelligent. Then they consider, ‘How unfortunate I am! I'm always engaged in sense gratification. I'm passing my days hankering for material enjoyment.’ This initial association with a great soul is also called association with the guru by hearing. By good fortune, at this time faith is awakened. When faith is awakened, one endeavors for devotional service.’ Then it is essential for one to take shelter of the lotus feet of a guru. In this way by good fortune persons with undeveloped intelligence become intelligent and take shelter of the lotus feet of a guru.

What type of guru one should take shelter of is explained in the sastras. One who has conquered the six enemies beginning with lust, one who is pure, one who performs devotional service on the path of raga, one who is brahminical, one who knows the clear path of the Vedas, one who sadhus can respect as guru, one who is able to control the senses, one who is merciful to all living entities, one who is cultured, one who is without duplicity, and one who is truthful-this type of householder is fit to be a guru. All these qualities are considered in two ways. The principle quality of a guru is attachment to Krishna and detachment for what is not related with Krishna. All other qualities are secondary. That is why Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu has said in the Chaitanya Charitamrta (Madhya 8.127):

lines: kiba vipra, kiba nyasi, sudra kene naya

blocks.text: ‘Whether one is a brahmana, a sannyasi, or a sudra regardless of what he is he can become a spiritual master if he knows the science of Krishna.’

If one possesses this principle symptom of a guru, then he is eligible to be guru even though he lacks one or two secondary symptoms. Being a brahmana and being a householder are counted as secondary symptoms. It is good if a person possesses these two secondary symptoms along with the principle qualification. But those who are defective in the principle symptom are unqualified to be guru even though they possess the other two. As stated in Sri Padma Purana:
